question: Why does app_fill refuse MobiumApp's volume slider on iOS, and how do I move it instead?
facts: On iOS that slider reports itself as a plain view with no trait and no value, so nothing outside the app can set it; fill is refused as unsupported.
The refusal names app_swipe: a drag from its thumb along its track moves it, as a finger does.
note: Needs the corpus pinned at or after mobium d263c6d (#209).

question: How do I set an <input type="range"> on a web page in a WebView?
facts: A range is a slider: app_fill takes a position from 0 to 1, set from the page's own min, max and step, so it lands exactly.
app_type on it is refused, naming app_fill; map names it by its label, with its value as its state.
note: Needs the corpus pinned at or after mobium d263c6d (#211).

question: How do I move one thumb of a two-thumb slider on a web page?
facts: Each thumb is its own slider in map: two ranges each by its label, or two ARIA sliders by theirs.
app_fill moves one thumb to a position from 0 to 1 — a range by its value, an ARIA slider by its arrow keys — and a thumb the page stops short fails as not_confirmed, saying so.
note: Needs the corpus pinned at or after mobium d263c6d (#211).

question: Why do some Mobium errors end with a line starting `next:`?
facts: An agent in Claude Code is handed a failed call's text alone, with no code and no structured remedy.
So an error's text is its message, then next: and its remedy when the message does not already say it; the structured payload keeps the two apart.
note: Needs the corpus pinned at or after mobium d263c6d (#212).
